question: During a festival season, an electric gadget marked at ₹ 5,000 is offered on sale at ₹ 4,250 after giving a certain discount. If discount percentage is reduced by 5%, at what price the electric gadget will be available to customers?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

According to the question, the discount percentage is reduced by 5%

So, The increase in selling price = 5% of the market price.

The final selling price = 4250 + [5000 × (5/100)] = 4250 + 250 = ₹ 4500

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Market price = ₹ 5000

Selling price = ₹ 4250

Discount reduced = 5%

**Formula used:**

Discount = M.P. - S.P.

Discount% = (Discount/M.P.) × 100

Where, M.P. = Market price

S.P. = Selling price

**Calculation:**

The initial discount = 5000 - 4250 = ₹ 750

The discount percentage = (750/5000) × 100 = 15%

The final discount = (15 - 5)% = 10%

The final selling price = (100 - 10)/100 × 5000 = ₹ 4500

**∴ The electric gadget will be available to customers at ₹ 4500**
